_hinweis: Content for /kursinhalte (src/pages/kursinhalte.astro, src/pages/kursinhalte/[level].astro, src/components/KursProgression.astro) and the lesson-plan generator (src/lib/stundenplan.js, which links each grammar line to a topic page by the English patterns in GRAMMAR_RULES). Everything here is our own, written from the CEFR can-do descriptors. Never copy from coursebooks: no unit titles, no tables of contents, no texts. `lehrwerke` would name coursebook series only ("goes with"), without a level after the name; the lists are empty for the English course until Edgar decides whether to name any (scripts/check-lehrwerk-leak.mjs fails the build on series + level). To add a level: insert an object in `niveaus` (order = order on the page and in the timeline); the id becomes the URL (/kursinhalte/<id>). `pruefung` only from B1 (Cambridge English, Trinity ISE, IELTS; see docs/content-plan.md §2). `selbstcheck`: exactly 5 sentences describing what a learner can do BEFORE this level.

probestunde._hinweis: Empty = an email to the contact address in src/lib/legal.js (there is no booking page yet). Once there is one, put its path here, e.g. "/probestunde". {niveau} is replaced by the level.

niveaus.label: A1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about yourself, your family and your day – in simple sentences.

kannZiele: You can introduce yourself: name, country, languages.
You can ask other people their name and where they are from.
You can spell your name.
You can say your phone number, address and age.
You can fill in a simple form.
grammatik: Yes/no questions with be (Are you …? Is it …?)

kannZiele: You can introduce your family.
You can say who belongs to you and how old they are.
grammatik: Possessive adjectives: my, your, his, her

kannZiele: You can describe your flat and your furniture.
You can say what you like and what you don't like.
grammatik: Adjectives after be (The kitchen is small.)
Prepositions of place: in, on, under, next to

kannZiele: You can ask for products and prices in a shop.
You can say what you like eating and drinking.
You can write a shopping list.
grammatik: Countable and uncountable nouns: some, any
wortschatz: Containers (a bottle of, a packet of)

kannZiele: You can describe your daily routine with times.
You can say how often you do something.
grammatik: Present simple: I work, she works
Adverbs of frequency: always, usually, never
Prepositions of time: at, on, in

kannZiele: You can talk about your hobbies.
You can say what you can and can't do.
You can ask others what they do in their free time.
grammatik: Present simple: questions and negatives (Do you …? I don't …)

selbstcheck: I can read and write the letters of the Latin alphabet.
I know a few words in English (hello, thank you, yes, no).
I can say my name in English.
I know the numbers from 1 to 10 in English.
I have some time each week to practise at home.
niveaus.selbstcheckNiedrig: No problem: A1.1 is the beginning, you don't need to know anything yet. In the trial lesson we look together at the best way for you to start.

niveaus.label: A1.2
niveaus.ziel: You get by in everyday life: in town, at the doctor's, in shops – and you say what you did.

kannZiele: You can ask the way and understand simple directions.
You can buy a ticket for the bus or the train.
grammatik: Imperatives: Turn left. Don't cross here.
Prepositions of place: next to, opposite, between
Wh- questions: How do I get to …?

kannZiele: You can say what hurts at the doctor's.
You can understand simple advice and instructions.
grammatik: Object pronouns: me, him, her, us, them

kannZiele: You can say what you did at the weekend.
You can ask others about their last holiday.
grammatik: Past simple: irregular verbs (went, saw, had)
wortschatz: Time words: yesterday, last week, ago

kannZiele: You can say what job you do and where you work.
You can say what you are doing at the moment.
grammatik: Present continuous (I'm working at the moment.)
a / an with jobs (She's a nurse.)

kannZiele: You can ask for clothes in a shop: size, colour, price.
You can compare two things and say which you prefer.
grammatik: Object pronouns: it, them (Can I try it on?)

kannZiele: You can say and understand dates.
You can invite someone and accept or say no politely.
grammatik: Ordinal numbers and dates (the third of May)
Prepositions of time: in, on, at

kannZiele: You can ask for information at a counter.
You can make a simple request politely.
grammatik: Polite requests: Could you …? Would you mind …?
Short answers: Yes, I do. No, I can't.

selbstcheck: I can introduce myself and ask others their name and where they are from.
I can understand numbers, prices and the time.
I can talk about my family.
I can ask for things in a shop.
I can describe my day with times.

niveaus.label: A2.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about the past, give reasons for your opinion and get by well when you travel.

kannZiele: You can talk about your childhood.
You can say what you could and couldn't do as a child.
grammatik: Past simple: questions and negatives (Did you …? I didn't …)

kannZiele: You can describe where things are in your home.
You can talk to a neighbour about a small problem.
grammatik: Prepositions of place and movement (into, out of, through)

kannZiele: You can give reasons: why you do a job, why you want to learn something.
You can talk about your duties at work.
grammatik: Phrasal verbs: the basics (fill in, look for)

kannZiele: You can talk about your interests and ask about other people's.
You can make plans for the weekend with a friend.
grammatik: Prepositions at the end (What are you interested in?)
-ing or to after verbs (enjoy cooking, want to learn)

kannZiele: You can compare different ways of living.
You can give simple tips about health.
grammatik: Zero and first conditional (If you …, you'll …)

kannZiele: You can say what you have already done and what you have never done.
You can ask for information politely.
grammatik: Present perfect: ever, never, just, already
Indirect questions: Can you tell me where …?
much, many, a lot of, a few, a little

kannZiele: You can book a room and ask about a trip.
You can talk about your holiday plans.
grammatik: Two objects: give me the key / give it to me

selbstcheck: I can say what I did at the weekend.
I can ask the way and understand the answer.
I can tell a doctor what hurts.
I can make or cancel an appointment.
I can say in a shop what I like and what fits me.

niveaus.label: A2.2
niveaus.ziel: You describe people and things in more detail, give advice and deal with offices and work.

kannZiele: You can describe a celebration in your country.
You can say what happened before and after something.
grammatik: Past simple of common irregular verbs

kannZiele: You can describe people: what they look like and what they are like.
You can say who is who: the woman who lives next door.
grammatik: Defining relative clauses: who, which, that
Order of adjectives (a lovely old house)

kannZiele: You can give advice and react to advice.
You can say what you would do in someone else's place.
grammatik: Second conditional: If I were you, I'd …

kannZiele: You can order something online and complain about a problem.
You can talk about prices and payment.
grammatik: the or no article (I like music / the music here)

kannZiele: You can talk about the weather and nature.
You can say what people do to protect the environment.
grammatik: The passive: present simple (Plastic is recycled.)

kannZiele: You can talk about your experience and how long you have done something.
You can write a short CV.
You can ask questions politely at an office.
You can say what you have had repaired or done.
grammatik: Indirect questions: Could you tell me if …?
have something done (I had my bike repaired.)

selbstcheck: I can talk about my childhood.
I can give reasons with because and so.
I can ask politely: Could you …? I'd like …
I can compare things: bigger than, the best.
I can talk about my hobbies (I'm interested in …).

niveaus.label: B1.1
niveaus.ziel: You talk about experiences, plans and opinions – also about topics that are less familiar.

kannZiele: You can tell a story from your life in the right order.
You can understand someone else's story in detail.
grammatik: Narrative tenses: past continuous and past perfect
Time clauses: after, before, while, as soon as
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Reading: texts about people's experiences
Trinity ISE I, Reading & Writing: long reading

kannZiele: You can describe your job and your plans for the future.
You can write a short email to a company.
grammatik: Defining relative clauses with prepositions (the company I work for)
Purpose: to, in order to, so that
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Writing Part 1: an email (about 100 words)
Trinity ISE I, Speaking: the topic task

kannZiele: You can give your opinion about media and the internet.
You can talk about something you have been doing for a while.
grammatik: Contrast: although, even though, despite, however
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Writing Part 2: an article or a story (about 100 words)

kannZiele: You can describe what happens at the doctor's or in hospital.
You can understand health information and announcements.
grammatik: The passive: present and past simple
Gerunds as subjects (Swimming is good for you.)
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Listening: announcements and short talks
Trinity ISE I, Speaking & Listening: independent listening

kannZiele: You can say what you would change about where you live.
You can make suggestions and agree on rules with others.
grammatik: Second conditional: If I had …, I would …
wish + past simple (I wish I had a garden.)
Suggestions: We could …, Why don't we …?
pruefung: Trinity ISE I, Reading & Writing: reading into writing
Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Writing Part 1: an email

kannZiele: You can plan a trip with others.
You can deal with problems on a journey.
grammatik: Future forms: will, going to, present continuous
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Speaking Part 3: planning something together
Trinity ISE I, Speaking: the conversation task

kannZiele: You can talk about friendship and family life.
You can describe a problem and ask for advice.
grammatik: 's or of (my sister's car, the end of the film)
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Speaking Part 4: a discussion

selbstcheck: I can talk about past events with the past simple and the present perfect.
I can give advice: You should … If I were you, I'd …
I can describe people and things with relative clauses (the man who …).
I can write a simple email to a company.
I can say when something happened with when, before and after.

niveaus.label: B1.2
niveaus.ziel: You discuss, describe processes and write clear texts – and you are ready for a B1 exam.

kannZiele: You can describe how something is made or done.
You can report what other people said.
grammatik: The passive with modals (It must be repaired.)
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Speaking Part 2: describing a photo
Trinity ISE I, Speaking: the topic task

kannZiele: You can talk about your learning and what you would do differently.
You can compare two options.
grammatik: Third conditional (introduction): If I had studied …
Paired conjunctions: both … and, either … or, neither … nor
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Reading: longer texts
Trinity ISE I, Reading & Writing: multi-text reading

kannZiele: You can report questions and requests.
You can talk about your town and how people live together.
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Listening: interviews and discussions

kannZiele: You can understand adverts and compare offers.
You can describe how things make you feel.
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Reading: matching people to texts

kannZiele: You can talk about changes at work and guess what will happen.
You can write a clear formal email.
grammatik: Time clauses: as soon as, until, by the time
Modals of deduction: must, might, can't
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Writing Part 1: an email
Trinity ISE I, Reading & Writing: extended writing

kannZiele: You can recommend a film, a book or an event.
You can talk about services you use.
grammatik: Confusing verbs: say / tell, borrow / lend
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary, Reading: opinions on a topic

kannZiele: You know every part of the exam and how long you have for it.
You can check your own texts for typical mistakes.
pruefung: Cambridge B1 Preliminary: all papers
Trinity ISE I: both modules

selbstcheck: I can tell a story in the right order (after, before, while).
I can give my opinion and support it with although and however.
I can describe simple processes in the passive.
I can write a complaint or a formal email.
I can plan a meeting or a trip with other people.

niveaus.label: B2.1
niveaus.ziel: You understand longer texts, argue convincingly and write in a formal style – at work and in study.

kannZiele: You can write a formal letter or email about a job.
You can compare jobs and working conditions.
grammatik: Formal linkers: whereas, while, given that
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Writing Part 2: a formal email or letter
Trinity ISE II, Reading & Writing: extended writing

kannZiele: You can understand opinion pieces and comments.
You can report what is said or believed without giving your own view.
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Reading: opinion texts
IELTS Academic, Reading

kannZiele: You can give a short talk about a topic.
You can add extra information about people and places.
grammatik: Non-defining relative clauses (My flat, which is small, …)
Participle clauses (introduction): people living in cities
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Speaking Part 2: comparing photos
Trinity ISE II, Speaking: the topic task

kannZiele: You can understand an interview about health.
You can describe causes and results.
grammatik: so … that, such … that, too, enough
Collocations: make a decision, take a risk
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Listening: interviews
IELTS, Listening

kannZiele: You can talk about regrets and different choices in the past.
You can write an essay with arguments for and against.
grammatik: Third conditional and wish (I wish I had …)
Modal perfects: should have, could have
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Writing Part 1: an essay (140–190 words)

kannZiele: You can understand factual texts about business.
You can describe a chart.
grammatik: Formal prepositions: due to, owing to, in view of
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Reading and Use of English: Parts 1–4
IELTS Academic, Writing Task 1: describing a chart

kannZiele: You can take part in a discussion and keep it going.
You can disagree politely and find a compromise.
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Speaking Part 3: the collaborative task
Trinity ISE II, Speaking: the collaborative task

selbstcheck: I have finished B1 or feel confident at B1.
I can describe processes in the passive, also with modal verbs.
I can use paired conjunctions (both … and, neither … nor).
I can give a talk on a topic for 3–4 minutes.
I understand the main points of the news on the radio.

niveaus.label: B2.2
niveaus.ziel: You write and speak precisely, also about abstract topics – and you are ready for a B2 exam.

kannZiele: You can talk about what will have happened by a certain time.
You can make careful guesses about the future.
grammatik: Future continuous and future perfect (By 2050 we will have …)
Modals of deduction: might, could, must, can't
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Speaking Part 4: discussion
Trinity ISE II, Speaking: the conversation task

kannZiele: You can understand factual texts about science.
You can explain how something works.
grammatik: The passive with modals and it is said that
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Reading: factual texts
IELTS Academic, Reading

kannZiele: You can understand a talk about a public issue.
You can report what people said, with the right reporting verb.
grammatik: Reported speech: reporting verbs (deny, suggest, admit)
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Listening: a talk

kannZiele: You can give a presentation about your culture.
You can write longer sentences in a natural way.
pruefung: Trinity ISE II, Speaking: the topic task

kannZiele: You can write a report or a review.
You can talk about different work cultures.
grammatik: Unreal past: as if, it's time, would rather
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Writing Part 2: a report or a review
IELTS, Writing Task 2: an essay (at least 250 words)

kannZiele: You can understand rules and regulations.
You can explain a contrast clearly.
grammatik: Contrast: although, even though, despite, in spite of
Paired conjunctions: not only … but also
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First, Reading and Use of English: key word transformations

kannZiele: You know every part of the exam and how long you have for it.
You can plan and check a text under time pressure.
pruefung: Cambridge B2 First: all papers
Trinity ISE II: both modules

selbstcheck: I can write formal emails without help.
I understand participle clauses (people living in cities).
I can turn verbs into nouns (decide – decision).
I can disagree in a discussion and suggest a compromise.
I understand newspaper articles on familiar topics.

niveaus.label: C1
niveaus.ziel: You understand demanding texts, speak spontaneously and fluently, and write well-structured texts.

kannZiele: You can understand academic texts and summarise them.
You can report claims with the right distance.
grammatik: Distancing: is said to, is believed to have
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Reading and Use of English
IELTS Academic, Reading

kannZiele: You can write a report or a proposal.
You can use formal phrases at work.
grammatik: Formal collocations: take into account, come into force
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Writing Part 2: a report or a proposal

kannZiele: You can argue about abstract topics and answer counter-arguments.
You can write a well-structured essay.
grammatik: Linkers for arguments: on the one hand … on the other, whereas, nevertheless
Inversion: Not only …, Never have I …
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Writing Part 1: an essay (220–260 words)
IELTS, Writing Task 2

kannZiele: You can understand lectures and broadcasts on most topics.
You can emphasise what matters in what you say.
grammatik: Reporting and distancing in texts (according to, allegedly)
Cleft sentences: What I need is …, It was … who …
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Listening
Trinity ISE III, Speaking & Listening: independent listening

kannZiele: You can work out the meaning of new words from their parts.
You can take part in a discussion naturally and smoothly.
grammatik: Verb prefixes: over-, under-, out-, re-, mis-
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Speaking Part 3: the collaborative task

kannZiele: You can give a structured talk on a complex topic.
You can switch between a formal and a more spoken style.
grammatik: Formal prepositions: regardless of, in view of, with regard to
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Speaking Part 2: the long turn
Trinity ISE III, Speaking: the topic task

kannZiele: You can write a review of a book, a film or an exhibition.
You can speculate about the past.
grammatik: Modal perfects: must have, might have, needn't have
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced, Writing Part 2: a review

kannZiele: You know every part of the exam and how long you have for it.
You can plan, write and check long texts under time pressure.
grammatik: Review: formal style and sentence structure
pruefung: Cambridge C1 Advanced: all papers
Trinity ISE III: both modules

selbstcheck: I have finished B2 or feel confident at B2.
I can report what other people said in reported speech.
I can argue about abstract topics and give counter-arguments.
I understand factual texts and talks on most topics.
I can switch between a formal and an informal style.
